---
title: "Getting started"
---


## Install

Two ways in. The Quarto way:

```sh
quarto add easyqda/easyQDA-quarto-theme
```

Or the way the zotQDA sites do it — **vendor the theme**: copy
`_extensions/` (and whatever else you use: `fonts/`, `offline/`,
`print/`) into your repository. Your site then builds without any
network access and without this repository existing, which is exactly
the property the theme is about. A small `update-theme.sh` that
re-copies from a sibling checkout keeps the vendored copy honest; qdaPy
and qdaR each carry one.

Then select the format in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
format:
  zotqda-theme-html: default
```

The format brings `toc`, `code-copy`, the light/dark theme pair and an
adaptive syntax-highlight pair (github / github-dark) with it. A
minimal working site lives in `examples/minimal/` — it is the site this
repository's CI renders and smoke-tests on every push.

## Self-hosted Noto Sans (optional)

Copy `fonts/` into the site project and declare it:

```yaml
project:
  resources:
    - fonts/
format:
  zotqda-theme-html:
    css: fonts/noto.css
```

The woff2 subsets keep their `unicode-range`, so a page only loads the
scripts it uses. Without this block the theme falls back to the system
font stack — still without any external request.

## Pin your Quarto version

Both the styling rules and the offline repairs are written against a
concrete Quarto version — currently **1.10.18**. Pin it in your build
script and treat upgrades as deliberate events;
[Maintenance and the Quarto pin](../dev/maintenance.qmd) describes the
procedure. The build script of this documentation refuses to run with
any other version unless explicitly told to:

```sh
PINNED="1.10.18"
ACTUAL="$(quarto --version)"
if [ "$ACTUAL" != "$PINNED" ] && [ -z "$ALLOW_UNPINNED_QUARTO" ]; then
  echo "quarto is $ACTUAL, pinned is $PINNED" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

## A complete site build

What the zotQDA sites run, reduced to one language:

```sh
quarto render mysite
python3 offline/postprocess.py mysite/_site   # the offline repairs
python3 offline/smoketest.py  mysite/_site    # headless-browser proof
python3 print/make_pdf.py mysite mysite/_site/docs.pdf   # optional
```

Each of the three steps has its own page here:
[Working offline](offline.qmd), [The docs as one PDF](pdf.qmd) — and
for a site in two languages, [Multilingual sites](multilingual.qmd).
